advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving the raw-propagation route: make run_workflow RAISE generation.PlanReviewCancelledStale and assert produce_plan_review_verdict catches it (gate_dispatch.py:225) and returns the plan-review-cancelled-stale INDETERMINATE.
evidence: gate_dispatch.py:225-229: `except generation.PlanReviewCancelledStale:` ... `return _cancelled_plan_review_verdict(ctx, cfg, scope=cancel)` with comment 'The batch (finders) path propagates step exceptions RAW ... unlike scripted ops (captured in-band) — accept both routes into the same cancelled verdict.'

test_plan_review_cancel.py:316-332: `_fake_run_workflow` itself catches `PlanReviewCancelledStale` and RETURNS a failed RunResult — the exception never propagates to the `except` at gate_dispatch.py:225; the test therefore exercises only the in-band route hitting line 235's `cancel.event.is_set()` branch.
ABSENCE: no test lets run_workflow raise PlanReviewCancelledStale out of produce_plan_review_verdict, so the 'accept both routes' claim in the comment is verified for only one of the two routes.
advisory.finding: The raw-exception propagation route into the cancelled verdict — the `except generation.PlanReviewCancelledStale` handler at gate_dispatch.py:225-229 — is untested. The only produce_plan_review_verdict cancel test exercises the in-band-capture route (a failed RunResult reaching the `event.is_set()` branch at line 235), so a regression that broke the raw-exception handler (letting the batch/finders-path exception escape as an unhandled error rather than a cancelled INDETERMINATE) would not be detected.
scenarios: A real run where the finders batch step raises PlanReviewCancelledStale raw (the documented batch-path behavior) instead of being captured in-band.
A future refactor that drops or narrows the except clause, letting the raw exception escape produce_plan_review_verdict.
